findings.title: Kept join results are wiped when a late device passes through an intermediate time keeper, so it shows its own "No match" for a join that worked
findings.why: electLeader calls earlyResults.clear() on every change of time keeper. When the old time keeper L and the next in line A both leave, and a late device C hears L's leave before A's (separate presence syncs), C first elects A, which clears the results it kept from B, the real new time keeper. Then C hears A leave and elects B with nothing to replay, and its own NO_MATCH_AFTER timer fires. B's 'joined' for C's push is lost, which breaks the ticket's acceptance ('whatever order it hears about the change in'). Kept layouts have the ask fallback (#95) to recover; kept results have none. The per-entry NO_MATCH_AFTER age check already handles staleness, so clearing the other senders' entries isn't needed. Repro: C shows 'nomatch C (own timeout)' instead of 'joined B-C'.

findings.title: A kept retry is dropped if any other device it names has left, though the same retry sent live is shown
findings.why: namesOnlyHere drops a kept retry when any device in p.devs has left, even though the retry still tells this device to try again. The device then shows its own 'No match' instead of the time keeper's 'Try again'. A live retry from the time keeper that names a device which has since left is still shown, so the two paths behave differently. The ticket's acceptance asks for the 'Try again' the new time keeper sent.

findings.title: The cap test allows up to 16 replayed results while EARLY_RESULTS is 8
findings.why: 'kept results are capped per device' asserts n <= 16, so it would still pass if the cap were doubled or applied wrongly. It should assert n === 8 (EARLY_RESULTS).
